reason: an estimator's repr shows only the parameters given non-default values, read from its __init__'s signature (inspect.signature, inspect.Parameter.empty), as scikit-learn's _changed_params

an estimator's parameters are its __init__'s parameters (inspect.signature), the basis of get_params, set_params, clone and the repr, as scikit-learn's BaseEstimator._get_param_names; inspect.isclass in clone
get_params reads each parameter, named by __init__'s signature, from the estimator itself (getattr(self, key)): the estimator API's definition
set_params sets a parameter named by the caller on the estimator itself (setattr(self, key, value)), after checking it is one of get_params' names: the estimator API's definition
check_is_fitted refuses a class (inspect.isclass); has_fit_parameter reads fit's signature (inspect.signature), as scikit-learn's
check_is_fitted(estimator, attributes): whether the estimator has each fitted attribute the caller names, as scikit-learn's _is_fitted
check_is_fitted without attributes: an estimator is fitted when one of its own attributes ends in an underscore (vars(estimator)), as scikit-learn's _is_fitted

check_random_state(None) returns NumPy's global RandomState itself, the one np.random.seed seeds (scikit-learn's np.random.mtrand._rand, a private name); the module functions' bound instance is that object
